ov: Twenty-one species of American mammals with a leathery, armoured shell and long digging claws. Only the three-banded armadillos can roll up into a ball.

why.ac: Nine-banded armadillos come out at night or dusk, foraging earlier on cold or cloudy days.
why.et: Nine-banded armadillos are hunted for meat in many rural areas.

len: 13–15 cm (pink fairy armadillo) to 150 cm (giant armadillo)
df: Mainly insects and other invertebrates dug from the soil; some species eat almost only ants and termites.
fx: The extinct car-sized glyptodonts, up to 2 tonnes, were true armadillos.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact (identical quadruplets) is confirmed: the nine-banded armadillo’s single fertilised egg splits into four identical embryos. No why.et: the sources don’t mention eating armadillos.
